name: Clearway Energy, Inc.
headquarters: 300 Carnegie Center, Suite 300, Princeton, New Jersey, United States
founded: 2012 (incorporated in Delaware as NRG Yield, Inc.; renamed Clearway Energy, Inc. in 2018)
employees: None — all employees transferred to Clearway Energy Group on 1 January 2025; CWEN is managed under a services agreement
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Clearway Energy, Inc. is a listed owner of contracted North American generation — about 13.9 GW rated across 27 states at 30 June 2026, of which roughly 11.1 GW is wind, solar and storage and 2.8 GW is California gas — and two things about it are commonly stated wrongly. It has a single listed share class: CWEN.A ceased to exist on 1 May 2026 when every Class A share converted into Class C, and any description of a CWEN/CWEN.A pair is stale. And it is not the same company as Clearway Energy Group, the private sponsor owned 50/50 by Global Infrastructure Partners (now part of BlackRock) and TotalEnergies, which does the development, employs the staff and offers assets down to CWEN for its independent directors to approve. BACKGROUND: FY2025 revenue $1,429m, net loss $(231)m, Adjusted EBITDA $1,217m and Cash Available for Distribution of $430m at the top of the original guidance range; the dividend has grown about 6.5% a year to $0.4750 a quarter. The battery fleet reached 1,439 MW rated / 849 MW net at 30 June 2026, of which 844 MW sits in California. In August 2026 the company cut 2026 CAFD guidance to $430–470m from $470–510m — its first cut in three years — blaming an El Niño wind shortfall that left CAISO wind at 87% of P-50. A material weakness in internal control over financial reporting, disclosed in January 2026 and unremediated at the year end, drew an adverse opinion from PwC.
ecosystemRole: We assess Clearway as the clearest listed read on what contracted renewables are worth to data-centre load, and as a structure that separates that exposure across two balance sheets. The hyperscaler contracts are originated at Clearway Energy Group — about 1.17 GW of Google PPAs across Missouri, Texas and West Virginia, 335 MW of Microsoft at Mount Storm, 520 MW at Royal Slope for a Washington utility serving data-centre growth — and reach the listed company only when a project is offered down and the independent directors approve it. For this ecosystem the useful comparison is with the merchant battery owners: Clearway's storage is almost entirely contracted on long tolls and resource-adequacy agreements rather than sold into ancillary markets, which is why its fleet is smaller than ENGIE's or AES's and its revenue far steadier.

productsAndServices.name: Utility-scale battery energy storage
productsAndServices.description: 1,439 MW rated / 849 MW net operating at 30 June 2026, up from 1,119 MW / 529 MW six months earlier. California is the largest single market at 844 MW rated — Arica 136 MW, Daggett 1 at 114 MW, Daggett 2 at 131 MW, Daggett 3 at 149 MW, Rosamond Central 147 MW, Rosamond South I 117 MW and Victory Pass 50 MW — but the growth has moved out of CAISO: the Honeycomb Portfolio added 320 MW / 1,280 MWh in Utah on 1 May 2026 under 20-year PacifiCorp tolling agreements, Pine Forest added 200 MW in ERCOT, and Hawaii carries 75 MW. Storage energy in MWh is disclosed for almost none of it.
highlights: Honeycomb Portfolio: four 80 MW projects totalling 320 MW / 1,280 MWh of four-hour Tesla batteries in Beaver and Iron Counties, Utah, on 20-year PacifiCorp tolls running to 2046; $605m of construction financing closed 11 March 2025; Rosendin was EPC

Spindle, under construction in Weld County, Colorado: 199 MW / 398 MWh of two-hour Tesla batteries for Public Service Company of Colorado, $261m financed 5 February 2026, Blattner as EPC, commercial operation targeted late 2026
Tesla Megapack 2 XL procurement announced 5 June 2025: a new 490 MW / 1,356 MWh order on top of an existing 520 MW / 1,680 MWh, all for 2026 delivery into the California and Colorado portfolios
Rosamond South II adds 92 MW in Kern County in the second half of 2026; Honeycomb Phase II offers a further 210 MW in Utah for 2027 at about $110m of corporate capital
Storage MWh is published for Honeycomb and Spindle only — CWEN's SEC filings state storage in megawatts alone, so every MWh figure for the California fleet in circulation is third-party
productsAndServices.positioning: A contracted storage owner rather than a merchant one, and mid-sized rather than large. S&P Global's US battery-owner table runs NextEra Energy Resources at 5.779 GW, ENGIE at 3.662 GW and AES at 1.978 GW; Clearway's 1.439 GW does not appear in that published table, and no independent tracker measures its fleet at owner level. Against Modo Energy's measured CAISO fleet of 16.2 GW in August 2026, Clearway's 844 MW of California storage is roughly 5%.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term tolling agreements and resource-adequacy contracts with regulated utilities and load-serving entities
targetSegments: Regulated utilities (PacifiCorp, Public Service Company of Colorado, SDG&E, SCE)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Rosamond South II 92 MW and Spindle 199 MW in the second half of 2026; Honeycomb Phase II 210 MW offered for 2027; Chimney Canyon, 975 MW of solar and storage in Arizona, offered for 2029

productsAndServices.name: Wind generation and repowering
productsAndServices.description: 4,234 MW rated / 3,713 MW net — the largest single technology in the fleet and the source of both the 2026 guidance miss and the clearest growth lever. The repowering programme applies to wind only: Goat Mountain went offline in February 2026 for a repower to 360 MW returning in the second half of 2027, Mt. Storm repowers to 335 MW in the second half of 2026, and Tuolumne and San Juan Mesa follow.
highlights: Alta I–V at 720 MW and Alta X–XI at 227 MW in Tehachapi, California, contracted to Southern California Edison to 2035 and 2038
Mesquite Sky, 340 MW in Callahan County, Texas — its legacy commodity contract was bought out on 27 March 2026 and replaced with a 15-year PPA with an investment-grade hyperscaler
Black Rock, 115 MW in West Virginia, sells to Toyota and Google to 2036
Elbow Creek, 122 MW in Howard County, Texas, hosts a co-located high-performance-computing data centre of about 122 MW of IT load
Wind capacity factor was 30.6% in FY2025 against 30.1% in FY2024, but Q2 2026 wind availability fell to 92%
productsAndServices.positioning: Repowering is how a yieldco grows without buying anything: the interconnection, land and permits are already owned, so the capital buys turbines and a restarted tax-credit clock rather than a queue position.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term power purchase agreements with utilities, corporates and hyperscalers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Mt. Storm and Tuolumne repowers complete in the second half of 2026; Goat Mountain and San Juan Mesa in the second half of 2027; about 1,871 MW of committed growth investment in total

productsAndServices.name: Utility-scale and distributed solar
productsAndServices.description: 4,730 MW rated / 2,889 MW net of utility-scale solar and 699 MW / 634 MW of distributed generation at 30 June 2026. The distributed business more than doubled on 30 March 2026 with the acquisition of the 613 MW Cardinal Portfolio from Deriva for $322m of net cash, in a co-investment partnership with Fengate.
highlights: Texas Solar Nova 1 and 2, 452 MW combined in Kent County, sell to Verizon to 2042
The Utah Solar Portfolio totals 530 MW, all contracted to PacifiCorp to 2036, and sits alongside the Honeycomb batteries
Conetoe, 80 MW in North Carolina, sells to Corning and Lockheed Martin to 2040
Solar generated 9,225 GWh in FY2025 against 8,658 GWh in FY2024, at a weighted-average capacity factor of 28.9%
98% of FY2025 total generation came from renewables and storage
productsAndServices.positioning: The steadiest part of the portfolio and the one with the least merchant exposure — weighted-average remaining contract duration across Renewables and Storage is about twelve years on a CAFD-weighted basis.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term PPAs; distributed generation through fund structures and co-investment partnerships
productsAndServices.roadmap: Swan Solar, 650 MW in Missouri on a 20-year Google PPA for 2028, and Royal Slope, 520 MW of solar and storage in Washington for 2027, are offered but not yet approved

productsAndServices.name: Flexible Generation — California gas
productsAndServices.description: 2,770 MW rated / 2,580 MW net, unchanged, and the segment most exposed to a contracting cliff. Marsh Landing at 820 MW, El Segundo at 546 MW, Carlsbad at 523 MW and Walnut Creek at 501 MW are all in CAISO selling resource adequacy; GenConn Devon and Middletown add 380 MW in Connecticut. Marsh Landing's and Walnut Creek's contracts run out between 2026 and 2030 and 2026 and 2027 respectively.
highlights: Segment Adjusted EBITDA of $210m in FY2025 on $291m of revenue — about 17% of group Adjusted EBITDA from 20% of rated capacity
Generation collapsed from 847 GWh in FY2024 to 323 GWh in FY2025: these are peaking and capacity assets, not baseload, and equivalent availability was 93.4%
El Segundo recontracted about 272 MW of resource adequacy across two 2025 sales, taking it to 100% contracted through 2027 and about 50% through 2028
No gas repowering is disclosed anywhere in the filings — the repowering programme is wind-only
productsAndServices.positioning: The part of the business a buyer discounts and a modeller has to watch: dispatchable California capacity is scarce and RA pricing has risen, but the contracts are short and the disclosure is thin.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bilateral resource-adequacy contracts with load-serving entities; tolling agreements
productsAndServices.roadmap: Marsh Landing and Walnut Creek recontracting from 2026 is the nearest material unknown; terms of the Q2 2026 agreements are not public

productsAndServices.name: The sponsor relationship — drop-downs and external management
productsAndServices.description: Clearway Energy, Inc. has no employees and no development arm. Clearway Energy Group originates and builds, then offers assets down; CWEN's independent directors review and approve each one. CWEN paid CEG about $23.8m under the Master Services Agreement in FY2025, and signed a Master Development Services Agreement with Clearway Renew on 22 December 2025 covering future approved repowerings.
highlights: There is no right-of-first-offer agreement: the strings 'right of first offer' and 'ROFO' appear zero times in the FY2025 10-K, and a dossier should not assert one exists
Nine drop-downs and third-party acquisitions closed across 2025 and 2026, from Rosamond South I at $33m to the Cardinal Portfolio at $322m net
The sponsor's late-stage pipeline as CWEN reports it grew from 11.2 GW in February 2026 to 13.5 GW in August 2026
Mt. Storm was sold to Clearway Renew for $152m in October 2025 so the sponsor could repower it, with CWEN agreeing to buy the repowered asset back for a $336m tax-equity Class B purchase
productsAndServices.positioning: A managed yieldco in substance: the listed vehicle supplies capital and a dividend, the sponsor supplies people, pipeline and origination, and the independent directors are the only check on transfer pricing between them.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not applicable — this is the corporate structure rather than a product
productsAndServices.roadmap: About 1,871 MW of committed growth investment and roughly $1.0bn of identified corporate capital across offered-but-unapproved projects

recentDevelopments.headline: 2026 guidance cut: CAFD to $430–470m from $470–510m and Adjusted EBITDA to $1,393–1,433m — the first cut in three years
recentDevelopments.read: An outturn, not a strategy change. The company attributes it to an El Niño wind shortfall rather than to contracting or cost, and the shares fell only 1.73% on a quarter that beat on earnings.

recentDevelopments.headline: Operational update discloses CAISO wind at 87% of P-50 and ERCOT at 98%, with second-quarter wind and solar about 5% below the level the guidance mid-point required
recentDevelopments.read: The clearest published statement of why a contracted portfolio still misses: the contracts are per-megawatt-hour, and the wind decides how many there are.

recentDevelopments.headline: Elbow Creek's legacy commodity contract bought out and replaced with a 15-year PPA with a commercial counterparty
recentDevelopments.read: The third contract restructuring of 2026, each structured as an in-substance financing that settles the old derivative liability over time — a repeatable value lever rather than a one-off.

recentDevelopments.headline: Langford's legacy contract replaced with a 15-year PPA with an investment-grade counterparty
recentDevelopments.read: Converts merchant Texas wind into contracted cash flow at the cost of a settlement liability.

recentDevelopments.headline: Class A shares convert one-for-one into Class C and CWEN.A is retired; Clearway Energy Group places 41,678,637 Class B shares in a Wilmington Trust voting trust
recentDevelopments.read: A single listed class from here. The voting trust must vote proportionally with all stockholders, which reproduces the pre-conversion 54.88/45.12 split exactly — the sponsor gave up nothing and the public gained liquidity.

recentDevelopments.headline: Honeycomb Portfolio reaches substantial completion — 320 MW / 1,280 MWh across four Utah projects on 20-year PacifiCorp tolls
recentDevelopments.read: The largest storage addition the company has made, and it is outside California.

recentDevelopments.headline: Cardinal Portfolio acquired from Deriva — 613 MW of distributed generation across eight states for $322m of net cash in a co-investment partnership with Fengate
recentDevelopments.read: More than doubles the distributed-solar fleet in one transaction and diversifies away from the utility-scale offtaker concentration.

recentDevelopments.headline: Mesquite Sky recontracted on a 15-year PPA with an investment-grade hyperscaler
recentDevelopments.read: The first of the three 2026 restructurings and the only one whose counterparty is described as a hyperscaler — direct data-centre revenue arriving at the listed company rather than the sponsor.

recentDevelopments.headline: 2026 proxy states plainly that Global Infrastructure Partners and TotalEnergies each own 50% of Clearway Energy Group through intermediate holding companies
recentDevelopments.read: The sponsor chain in the company's own words. BlackRock's absorption of GIP changed the filer name, not the chain or the percentages.

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025 results: revenue $1,429m, net loss $(231)m, Adjusted EBITDA $1,217m, CAFD $430m at the top of the original guidance range; dividend per share $1.77
recentDevelopments.read: Net loss and record CAFD in the same year is normal for this structure — depreciation and tax-equity allocations drive the GAAP line while cash distributions drive the dividend.

recentDevelopments.headline: Spindle financing closes at $261m for 199 MW / 398 MWh in Colorado
recentDevelopments.read: A second non-California storage market and a two-hour product, against Honeycomb's four.

recentDevelopments.read: Terming out revolver borrowings at a coupon two points above the 2031 and 2032 notes — the cost of capital has moved against the sector since those were issued.

relationships.scale: 490 MW / 1,356 MWh ordered on top of an existing 520 MW / 1,680 MWh
relationships.note: Tesla is the battery supplier across the Honeycomb, California and Colorado storage portfolios.
relationships.context: Clearway announced the incremental Megapack 2 XL order on 5 June 2025, bringing total ordered volume to just over a gigawatt with all deliveries scheduled in 2026 for the California and Colorado portfolios. The units are built in Lathrop, California with cells partly from Sparks, Nevada, which matters for domestic-content adders under the tax credits. Honeycomb's 320 MW / 1,280 MWh in Utah and Spindle's 199 MW / 398 MWh in Colorado are both Tesla-equipped, at four hours and two hours respectively.

relationships.note: Rosendin was the EPC contractor on the four-project Honeycomb storage portfolio in Utah.
relationships.context: Named in Clearway Energy Group's March 2025 financing release for the $605m Honeycomb package. The portfolio reached substantial completion on 1 May 2026 and had already been dropped down to the listed company in October 2025, so the construction relationship sits with the sponsor while the asset sits with Clearway Energy, Inc. Rosendin's own dossier records roughly 10 GWh of installed battery EPC across the ecosystem, of which this is one of the larger single portfolios.

relationships.note: Blattner Energy is the EPC on the Spindle battery project in Weld County, Colorado.
relationships.context: Spindle is a 199 MW / 398 MWh two-hour Tesla installation contracted to Public Service Company of Colorado, financed at $261m in February 2026 and targeted for commercial operation in late 2026. Blattner's own dossier lists repeat-owner frameworks with Pattern, Orsted, RWE, Recurrent and NextEra and records that on Blattner sites the owner furnishes the batteries — consistent with Clearway having procured the Tesla units directly under its own Megapack order rather than through the contractor.

relationships.scale: about 1.17 GW across three PPAs; 1.24 GW including an existing West Virginia contract
relationships.via: Long-term power purchase agreements originated by Clearway Energy Group
relationships.note: Google is the counterparty to a portfolio of three 2025 power purchase agreements across Missouri, Texas and West Virginia, announced on 15 January 2026.
relationships.context: The partnership totals about 1.24 GW and more than $2.4bn of infrastructure investment, serving Google data centres in SPP, ERCOT and PJM. The distinction that matters is which balance sheet holds it: the PPAs were originated at Clearway Energy Group, and only the Goat Mountain repower — 360 MW on a 15-year Google PPA for the second half of 2027 — has been committed to the listed company. Swan Solar, 650 MW in Missouri on a 20-year Google PPA for 2028, and Catamount in West Virginia have been offered to Clearway Energy, Inc. but not yet approved by its independent directors. Separately, Google is already an offtaker at the 115 MW Black Rock wind farm alongside Toyota, to 2036.

relationships.via: 20-year power purchase agreement at Mount Storm
relationships.note: Microsoft holds a 20-year power purchase agreement for 335 MW at the Mount Storm wind farm in West Virginia.
relationships.context: Clearway paid roughly $35m in May 2025 and a further $39m in July 2025 to buy out Mount Storm's legacy offtake hedge ahead of the Microsoft agreement — the cost of clearing a merchant position to make room for a contracted one. Mount Storm is being repowered to 335 MW for the second half of 2026, with the listed company agreeing a $336m tax-equity Class B purchase to acquire the repowered asset after having sold it to Clearway Renew for $152m in October 2025 so the sponsor could carry out the work.

relationships.via: Storage offtake with Public Service Company of Colorado
relationships.note: Public Service Company of Colorado, an Xcel Energy operating utility, is the offtaker for the Spindle battery project.
relationships.context: Spindle is a two-hour, 199 MW / 398 MWh Tesla installation in Weld County targeted for late 2026. Worth stating precisely because the market has misreported it: at least one trade outlet attributed a 200 MW Colorado storage contract to Microsoft, and the counterparty is the regulated utility, not a hyperscaler. Xcel's own dossier records its Colorado storage procurement from the buyer's side.

relationships.note: Constellation Energy Generation is the offtaker at the 55 MW Dan's Mountain wind farm in Maryland, to 2037.
relationships.context: Dan's Mountain reached commercial operation in May 2025 in Allegany County, Maryland, and is held 50%. The contract runs to 2037. It is a small position but a clean example of the portfolio's structure — a competitive retail and wholesale supplier buying contracted renewable output rather than a utility or a hyperscaler.

relationships.note: Both own large contracted US renewables and storage fleets; S&P Global's US battery-owner table places NextEra first at 5.779 GW, where Clearway's 1.439 GW does not appear.
relationships.context: A ranking comparison rather than a commercial relationship. The useful contrast is structural: NextEra Energy Resources is the development arm of a regulated utility holding company and retains what it builds, while Clearway Energy, Inc. is an externally managed listed vehicle that buys finished assets from a sponsor and has no employees of its own. Both compete for the same hyperscaler PPAs — NextEra directly, Clearway through Clearway Energy Group's origination team.

relationships.note: Both are contracted US renewables and storage owners selling to hyperscalers; S&P Global measures AES at 1.978 GW of operating batteries against Clearway's 1,439 MW rated / 849 MW net.
relationships.context: The closest peer on storage scale in the covered set, and the comparison exposes the ownership question. Clearway reports storage at both rated and net capacity because most of the California fleet sits in partnerships at 25% to 50% — 844 MW rated becomes 391 MW net. A rated-to-rated comparison with AES therefore flatters Clearway, and a net comparison is the honest one. Both companies also sit on the buyer side of the same hyperscaler demand, AES through Amazon and Microsoft and Clearway through Google and Microsoft.

relationships.note: Both own California and Texas generation and appear together in independent storage-completion rankings; Vistra's dossier records Clearway among the top ten owners by megawatts brought online in 2023 on an Enverus table.
relationships.context: A ranking co-appearance rather than a commercial relationship, and it is recorded as such on both sides. The businesses are structurally opposite: Vistra is an integrated merchant with a five-million-customer retail book hedging its generation, while Clearway sells essentially all of its output on long-term contracts and holds no retail position. That difference is why Vistra's storage revenue swings with market prices and Clearway's does not, and it is the more instructive comparison than the megawatt counts.

policyExposure.regime: ITC/45X (One Big Beautiful Bill Act phase-out)
policyExposure.exposure: Clearway's growth programme depends on tax credits monetised through tax-equity partnerships, and those partnerships are the subject of the company's disclosed material weakness in internal control. The FY2025 10-K carries the credit regime through the committed growth investments — about 1,871 MW of repowering and new build — where a repowered wind farm can restart credit eligibility. Tax-equity allocations drive the gap between a $(231)m net loss and $430m of cash available for distribution.
policyExposure.mitigation: Repowering is itself the mitigation: Goat Mountain, Mt. Storm, Tuolumne and San Juan Mesa reuse existing interconnections and land rights while restarting the credit clock, which is why the committed programme is wind repowering rather than greenfield.

policyExposure.exposure: The 2,770 MW Flexible Generation fleet earns from selling resource adequacy into CAISO rather than from generating — 323 GWh produced in FY2025 against 847 GWh in FY2024. Marsh Landing's contracts expire between 2026 and 2030 and Walnut Creek's between 2026 and 2027, so a material share of the segment's $210m of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA is exposed to recontracting terms that are not public.
policyExposure.mitigation: El Segundo recontracted about 272 MW across two sales in January and February 2025, taking it to 100% contracted through 2027 and about 50% through 2028; the company signed further Marsh Landing and Walnut Creek agreements in the second quarter of 2026 whose tenor, price and megawatts have not been disclosed.

policyExposure.exposure: Just over a gigawatt of Tesla Megapack 2 XL capacity is on order for 2026 delivery, built in Lathrop, California with cells sourced partly from Sparks, Nevada. Domestic assembly and cell sourcing bear directly on domestic-content adders and on foreign-entity restrictions, and Clearway's single-supplier concentration on Tesla for storage is the corresponding risk.
policyExposure.mitigation: Company-published sourcing detail is limited to the Lathrop and Sparks statements in the June 2025 procurement release; no first-party domestic-content percentage or foreign-entity analysis was located.

policyExposure.exposure: PwC issued an adverse opinion on internal control over financial reporting as of 31 December 2025. The weakness is in the review of hypothetical-liquidation-at-book-value calculations used to allocate net income and loss to redeemable non-controlling interests and non-controlling interests in tax-equity partnerships — the exact mechanism through which the tax-credit economics reach the income statement. It was unremediated at the year end.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company disclosed the weakness itself in an 8-K on 7 January 2026 and revised the first three quarters of 2025 immaterially; the corrections had no impact on net income, loss or cash flow from operations.

financials.commentary: Two structural features make this income statement hard to read. Depreciation of $682m and tax-equity allocations under hypothetical-liquidation-at-book-value accounting drive a GAAP net loss while cash available for distribution funds a growing dividend — a $(231)m FY2025 net loss and a record $430m of CAFD are the same year. And no published analyst consensus exists for CAFD or CAFD per share, the metrics management guides to and the dividend is set from; consensus exists only for EPS and revenue, so any CAFD 'beat' or 'miss' is measured against company guidance alone.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that two widely repeated descriptions of this company are now wrong, and both matter for anyone modelling it. There is one listed share class, not two: every Class A share converted into Class C at 12:01 a.m. on 1 May 2026, CWEN.A was suspended on the NYSE and a Form 25-NSE was filed. And there is no right-of-first-offer agreement — the strings 'right of first offer' and 'ROFO' appear zero times in the FY2025 10-K, which is a real change from the NRG Yield-era structure. What operates instead is an offer-and-approve process in which the sponsor offers and the independent directors decide.

(High confidence) We assess the sponsor conversion was designed to change liquidity without changing control, and succeeded. Basis: post-conversion voting power is Class B 39.48%, Class C 45.12% and Class D 15.40% — reproducing the pre-conversion 54.88/45.12 sponsor-versus-public split exactly — because Clearway Energy Group simultaneously placed 41,678,637 Class B shares into a Wilmington Trust voting trust whose trustee must vote in the same proportion as all stockholders. The public got a single, deeper class; the sponsor gave up no relative votes.

(High confidence) We assess the storage fleet is contracted rather than merchant, and that this is the correct frame for comparing it with the ERCOT battery owners. Basis: Honeycomb's 320 MW / 1,280 MWh sits on 20-year PacifiCorp tolling agreements to 2046, Spindle's 199 MW / 398 MWh is contracted to Public Service Company of Colorado, and the California fleet sells resource adequacy to SDG&E, SCE and other load-serving entities on contracts running to 2033–2041. None of it earns from ancillary-services arbitrage, which is why its revenue did not move when ERCOT ancillary prices collapsed.

(High confidence) We assess the 'large CAISO storage fleet' framing understates the shift that has already happened. Basis: California is still the largest single storage market at 844 MW rated, but only 391 MW net, and every megawatt of 2026 growth landed elsewhere — Honeycomb's 320 MW in Utah, Pine Forest's 200 MW in ERCOT, Spindle's 199 MW in Colorado, against 92 MW at Rosamond South II in California. Against Modo Energy's measured 16.2 GW CAISO fleet, Clearway's California storage is roughly 5%.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the hyperscaler exposure is real but sits mostly at the sponsor, and that the gap between the two balance sheets is the single most important thing to track. Basis: about 1.17 GW of Google PPAs, 335 MW of Microsoft at Mount Storm and 520 MW at Royal Slope were all originated at Clearway Energy Group; of these only the Goat Mountain repower is committed to the listed company, while Swan Solar, Catamount and Royal Slope are offered and unapproved. The listed company's own direct data-centre revenue today is the Mesquite Sky 15-year hyperscaler PPA signed in March 2026 and Goat Mountain from 2027.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the gas fleet is the nearest material unknown and is under-disclosed. Basis: Marsh Landing's contracts expire between 2026 and 2030 and Walnut Creek's between 2026 and 2027, together 1,321 MW of the 2,770 MW segment that produced $210m of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA; the company signed new resource-adequacy agreements for both in the second quarter of 2026 and published no tenor, price or megawatt figure. California RA pricing has risen, so the terms could move the segment materially in either direction and nothing in the public record fixes them.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the 2026 guidance cut is a weather outcome rather than a business deterioration, while noting the structure that makes weather bite. Basis: the company's own operational update attributes it to an El Niño pattern leaving measured CAISO wind at 87% of P-50 and ERCOT at 98%, with second-quarter wind and solar about 5% below the guidance mid-point requirement; long-term targets of $2.90 to $3.10 of CAFD per share by 2030 were reaffirmed at the same time, and the second quarter beat on both earnings and revenue. A portfolio contracted per megawatt-hour rather than per megawatt of capacity carries the resource risk itself.

(Low confidence) We assess the material weakness in internal control is a diligence item rather than an accounting problem, but it sits in an uncomfortable place. Basis: PwC's adverse opinion concerns hypothetical-liquidation-at-book-value calculations allocating income to tax-equity partnerships, the immaterial revisions it produced left net income and operating cash flow untouched, and the company disclosed it itself. Cutting against that comfort: HLBV allocation is precisely the mechanism through which the tax-credit economics reach the income statement, and it explains the $(400)m allocated away from Clearway Energy, Inc. in FY2025. It was unremediated at the year end.

Collection gap: storage energy capacity is not published for most of the fleet. Clearway's SEC filings state storage in megawatts only, and MWh appears in first-party sources for Honeycomb (1,280 MWh) and Spindle (398 MWh) alone. No MWh figure exists in any first-party source for Arica, the three Daggett projects, Rosamond Central, Rosamond South I, Victory Pass, Pine Forest, Mililani I or Waiawa, so every MWh figure for the California fleet in circulation is third-party.

Collection gap: no independent tracker measures Clearway's battery fleet at owner level. S&P Global's published US battery-owner table runs NextEra Energy Resources, ENGIE and AES and does not include Clearway; Modo Energy publishes market totals but names no owners; Wood Mackenzie's published rankings measure integrators rather than owners; and the American Clean Power Association's owner data is members-only. The 1,439 MW figure is the company's own, corroborated only by summing its published project table.

Collection gap: no published analyst consensus exists for cash available for distribution or CAFD per share in any period, which are the metrics management guides to and the dividend is set from. Consensus exists for earnings per share and revenue only. Any statement that Clearway 'beat' or 'missed' on CAFD is measured against its own guidance, not against the market.
